payload.value: shipped: the landing folds every shard, the spec line is true against the code, and the foreign-dirt refusal is asserted to leave a shard alone

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a session ends on a user correction and a self-caught false claim, I want the cause written into the always-on guidance rather than into a summary, so I can stop the next session repeating it.

Finding 1, user-corrected. The sharding design put both the writer identity and the compaction in src/basicly/merge.py. The owner asked whether the tracker can also be installed without basicly in a consumer repository, and it can: a standalone consumer would have taken the file-count cost of sharding and received none of the merge safety, because neither half existed for them. The kit's own SPEC.md line 3 already says it serves a reader who has only the kit, so the rule existed and was not applied. The failure was reading the engine seam before the kit's own contract.

Finding 2, self-caught late. SPEC.md section 4.0 was written in the same commit that shipped sharding and asserted 'The engine's landing calls the same function'. No such call existed. docs-claims passed because it catches an invented command and not a claim about a call, and compaction was run by hand three times before the gap was seen.

Not filed as findings, recorded so the branch not taken is on the record. The seam violation caught by test_gate_source and the two faulty instruments (git stash -u restoring a deleted .gitattributes, and a .git size accumulated across benchmark rounds) were all caught by controls that already exist and fired. They need no new control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- core-rules carries a bullet requiring a change under .basicly/core/kit/ to name where a consumer with no engine gets the capability.
- quality-gate carries a bullet naming a design-document sentence about a call as a claim rather than a plan.
- Both fragments project into the agent instruction files and basicly check reports no drift.
payload.title: carry the two retro findings from the sharding session into the catalog
